text:
emma: quick flag from bronco-v1 int8 bring-up — noticed fullwidth colon (U+FF1A) used in zh-code-mixed docs is being converted to ASCII ':' in canary outputs. breaks markdown/code samples and leads to downstream lint failures (doc-renderer tests).

ryan: repro'd locally. fp16 keeps U+FF1A, int8 canary output shows ':'. pre-tokenization ids identical. snippet below.

```
# repro (utf8 terminal)
echo -n "调用： foo()" | ./infer --model bronco-v1 --quant int8 --input -
# output-int8: 调用: foo()
# output-fp16: 调用： foo()
```

li: token ids before inference are the same when we run our tokenizer binary. so looks like post-gen normalization (detok/postproc) converting fullwidth punctuation to ASCII for compatibility heuristics.

anya: which postproc image does the int8 canary use? if it's a pinned compat image that normalizes fullwidth punctuation, that would explain the delta.

ryan: int8 canary manifest uses `postproc:2024-07-compat`. fp16 baseline used `postproc:main`. the compat branch has a normalize-punct flag that maps fullwidth->ASCII. bad for code/docs.

emma: bypassed postproc locally (naive join) and fullwidth colon preserved, doc lint passes. confirming postproc is the culprit.

anya: plan: (1) open small detok/postproc PR to avoid mapping U+FF1A when adjacent to CJK or in code spans; (2) temporarily point bronco int8 canary to `postproc:main` for the smoke; (3) add a unit test for fullwidth punctuation in the detok suite and add a sample to multilingual dev bundle. also add a manifest lint to flag postproc tags older than main for models serving docs/code locales.

ci-bot: [CI] postproc PR #612 started  running 7 tests

li: PR includes a preserve_fullwidth_punct test and a small heuristic (preserve if adjacent to CJK or inside inline code markers).

ci-bot: [CI] postproc PR #612 passed  7 tests :white_check_mark:

ryan: updated canary to postproc:main and re-ran bronco int8 smoke — docs lint and rendering recovered.

emma: great triage. follow-ups: add fullwidth punctuation cases (FF01..FF5E) to the locale smoke matrix and note in the onboarding doc that postproc normalization can affect code/docs in mixed-script locales. will keep an eye on other fullwidth/halfwidth mappings. :thumbsup:
